artifacts.summary: Confirms the four-hop aux carrier chain defect and the implement-readmission gap against the live source store, recommends confirm-then-clear (Item 1) and a post-triage chain-state override placed in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh rather than orchestrate-triage-classify.sh (Item 2), and corrects the dispatch's own premise about where the multi-task state file is read.

next_steps: Run /orchestrate 547 to create an implementation plan

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-triage-classify.sh reads only specs/state.json and a candidate's own .orchestrator-handoff.json (its own header states this read set explicitly). The per-invocation multi-task state file (specs/.orchestration/.orchestrator-multi-state-{session_id}.json, holding aux_pending/blocker_escalation_count/etc.) is loaded only inside orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh itself via mt_get/mt_set/mt_save. A routing predicate that needs to key on aux_pending or similar chain state must be placed as a post-triage override inside orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (after triage_group[$t] is assigned, before the forced-phase/effective_group loop), never inside orchestrate-triage-classify.sh, to avoid widening that script's documented narrow read contract.

The .orchestrator-handoff.json schema's next_action_hint field is confirmed structurally dead in the agent-system source store: zero agent files write it (verified by grep across general-implementation-agent.md, reviser-agent.md, lean-implementation-agent.md), and test-handoff-reader-parity.sh's own header states it was retired from that suite because neither field has a live reader any more. A future routing need should not assume next_action_hint has any adoption to build on -- treat it as greenfield, not as an existing signal to tap.

blocker_escalation_count[t] in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's multi-task state resets to 0 each /orchestrate invocation (per orchestrate-loop-guard-init.sh's own comment), and increments only when a blocker-research fork is actually built and dispatched (not on confirmed failure). When redesigning a confirm-then-clear remedy for a similar aux-chain carrier, the increment point can usually stay put -- only the aux_pending clear point needs to move from emission time to confirmation time, provided the carrier-success branch is also updated to perform the clear that the emission-time write no longer does.
